items.title: Large-Market Discipline in Combinatorial Double Auctions: No Assembly, Bundle Selection, and Complementarities
items.desc: Designs combinatorial buyer's-bid double auctions for markets in AI assets — data, model weights, and fine-tuned models — where a "No Assembly" constraint prevents platforms from combining components supplied by different sellers, and establishes large-market incentive discipline. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-06]

items.title: The Institutional Window: Occupation- and Jurisdiction-Specific Calibration of Liability Signaling for Preserved Human Fallback Capability
items.desc: Models how generative AI collapses the classical cost-based quality signal in expert services, leaving outcome-contingent liability commitments as the only way for competent providers to separate themselves — and studies how such commitments certify a perishable human fallback capability. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-08-06]

items.title: Cross-Sectional Heterogeneity in LSTM Networks for Financial Time Series
items.desc: Studies how cross-sectional heterogeneity across assets limits standard LSTM architectures for return prediction in low signal-to-noise financial time series, and proposes accounting for it explicitly. [arXiv q-fin.ST, posted 2026-08-06]

items.title: Counterfactual Analysis via Large Language Models
items.desc: Investigates LLMs (GPT-3.5) for counterfactual analysis in online lending, predicting counterfactual return on investment under hypothetical scenarios to support lending decisions. [arXiv cs.AI / q-fin.GN, posted 2026-08-05]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Online Resource Allocation with Convex-Set Machine-Learned Advice
items.desc: Golrezaei, Jaillet, and Zhou propose a framework that uses machine-learned demand predictions ("advice") represented as convex sets to improve online resource-allocation decisions while staying robust to prediction inaccuracy. [Operations Research, published online 2026-08-06]

items.title: Why AI is a risk to Communist China
items.desc: Cover leader arguing China is adopting AI fast but is less well placed to benefit than many assume: autocracy brings some advantages in diffusing AI through the economy, but also serious economic and social problems. [Economist, 2026-08-06]

items.title: How AI is breaking the British state
items.desc: On "agentic flooding": citizens armed with AI models and agents are inundating bureaucracies with claims, objections, and appeals — employment-tribunal backlogs up 55% in a year — threatening to overwhelm government operations built for the age of post and telephone. [Economist, 2026-08-06]

items.title: What's Behind the A.I. Shake-Up at Google
items.desc: DealBook on Google's AI leadership reshuffle: Demis Hassabis becomes Alphabet chief scientist and DeepMind chair, Koray Kavukcuoglu takes over day-to-day DeepMind management, and Jeff Dean leaves to found a startup — amid investor anxiety over roughly $200 billion in AI capex and lagging models. [NYT, 2026-08-06]
